description: Somos un equipo multidisciplinario enfocado en construir una solución tecnológica completa, sólida e innovadora. Combinamos la arquitectura de software, el desarrollo de plataformas web interactivas y un diseño visual atractivo para crear un producto con verdadero impacto.
summary:
WillAI is an early warning and tactical response platform engineered to predict, detect, and combat wildfires across the high-altitude Andes (Parinacochas, Ayacucho, Peru).

We developed a unified system connecting an offline-first bilingual mobile app (Quechua-Spanish) for indigenous rural communities with a real-time command center for emergency operators. WillAI directly addresses the challenge by fusing NASA Earth Observations—specifically NASA FIRMS thermal anomalies from VIIRS (375m) and MODIS (1km)—with an Andean-calibrated Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) and an elliptical propagation simulator that accounts for rugged topography (Copernicus 30m DEM), wind vectors, and natural road and river firebreaks.

Traditional fire systems fail in the Andes due to steep terrain, communication dead zones, and language barriers. WillAI bridges this divide: comuneros can submit georeferenced offline reports in their native language, while firefighters visualize multi-sensor fused burn scars, date, duration to dispatch brigades preemptively. By transforming space intelligence into grassroots action, WillAI protects vital highland water basins and vulnerable Andean lives.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

WillAI is an end-to-end wildfire intelligence and early response system operating across three interconnected layers:

  1. Satellite Ingestion & Multi-Sensor Fusion: WillAI consumes near-real-time (NRT) and historical thermal anomaly streams from NASA FIRMS, unifying high-resolution VIIRS (375m from NOAA-20, NOAA-21, and Suomi-NPP) and MODIS (1km from Terra and Aqua), supplemented by official SERFOR Peru MapServer records. To prevent visual clutter and false multi-reporting, we built a spatial-temporal dissolving algorithm: raw sensor footprints are projected into UTM Zone 18S, clustered by day, and dissolved across a 1,200-meter metric proximity threshold. This yields clean polygonal ground footprints that calculate the exact affected land in square meters (m2m^2m2) and hectares, the exact incident date, and the fire duration derived from satellite orbital timestamps.
  2. High-Altitude Fire Danger & ML Susceptibility: Because the standard boreal Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index (FWI) fails in Andean ecosystems, WillAI calibrates the FWI specifically to the high-altitude pajonal altoandino (3,200–4,800 m.a.s.l.), achieving an empirical PR-AUC of 0.7816, ROC-AUC of 0.8029, and a calibrated Brier Score of 0.1789 (a 39.8% error reduction over standard models). In parallel, a Platt-calibrated Random Forest classifier predicts territorial occurrence risk across a 265-cell grid covering the eight districts of Parinacochas using topography, moisture, wind, fuel dryness, and proximity to settlements.
  3. Physical Andean Propagation Simulator: An elliptical propagation engine (inspired by Cell2Fire and implemented in pure Python) runs Dijkstra shortest-path calculations on an 8-connected grid. It integrates Copernicus 30m DEM slope corrections, Open-Meteo wind vector forecasts with a ±15∘\pm 15^\circ±15∘ stochastic uncertainty ensemble, and dynamically halts fire spread along 91 unpaved mountain roads (trochas carrozables) and river networks acting as natural physical firebreaks.
  4. Bilingual Offline-First Mobile Client: Rural citizens and volunteer brigades use an Expo/React Native app with local SQLite storage. When connectivity drops in remote mountain valleys, users record evidence (GPS coordinates accurate to ±3\pm 3±3m, photos, and up to 15 seconds of video) and receive voice-guided escape routes in Quechua Chanka ("Qata wichayman amapuni asuykuychu"). Data synchronizes automatically via multipart HTTP queues once an internet uplink is detected.
  5. Tactical Command Center Web SPA: A dark-themed React/TypeScript dashboard built for municipal emergency managers (COEP/COEL/OGRD) and Fire Station B-12. It provides unit dispatch vectors, legal closure records with PDF export, and one-click GIS packaging (QGIS .zip project and 3D Google Earth .kmz extrusions).

2. What benefits does it have?

  • True Ground Footprint Measurement: Replaces deceptive pulsating point dots with precise multi-sensor fused polygons displaying exact damaged terrain in m2m^2m2.
  • Predictive Tactical Horizon: Generates 1-hour, 3-hour, and 6-hour fire spread isochrones, enabling commanders to deploy firebreaks ahead of the flame front rather than reacting after ignition has peaked.
  • Zero-Connectivity Reliability: Functions completely offline in deep mountain ravines, guaranteeing that critical alerts and citizen observations are never lost.
  • Linguistic Inclusion: Overcomes the language barrier by delivering bidirectional emergency communication in Quechua Chanka, engaging indigenous populations historically excluded from technological disaster platforms.
  • Vulnerable Asset Protection: Cross-references fire propagation vectors against rural cadastral registries to identify dwellings, schools, and livestock corrals within a 5 km exposure buffer.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Headwater Ecosystem Conservation: Protects high-altitude peatlands (bofedales) and water catchments that supply drinking and irrigation water to tens of thousands of inhabitants downstream in arid southern Peru.
  • Drastic Reduction in Response Times: Shrinks the detection-to-dispatch loop from hours (or days) down to minutes, allowing B-12 firefighters and communal brigades to neutralize ignitions before they evolve into catastrophic crown fires.
  • Democratizing Enterprise GIS: Delivers high-level spatial decision support to resource-constrained provincial municipalities, replacing expensive proprietary GIS software with open, calibrated space intelligence.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend & Web GIS: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, Lucide Icons, Custom SVG Cartography, Vanilla CSS with custom tactical styling.
  • Mobile Development: React Native, Expo SDK 58, TypeScript, expo-sqlite, expo-location, expo-video, expo-notifications, Zustand state management.
  • Backend & APIs: Python 3.11, Django 5.1, Django REST Framework, Celery asynchronous queue, Redis.
  • Spatial Processing & Machine Learning: PostGIS, Shapely, PyProj, GeoDjango, NumPy, SciPy, Scikit-learn (RandomForestClassifier, CalibratedClassifierCV with Platt sigmoid scaling).
  • External Data & Earth Observations: NASA FIRMS API (VIIRS 375m NRT/Archive: NOAA-20, NOAA-21, Suomi-NPP; MODIS 1km: Terra/Aqua), Copernicus DEM GLO-30, Open-Meteo Weather Forecast & Historical Archive APIs, SERFOR Peru ArcGIS MapServer, MTC / IGN National Road Network, ANA Hydrographic River Basins.
  • Interoperability Formats: GeoJSON, Shapefile/QGIS Package (.qgs), Google Earth KMZ 3D with thermal extrusions.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Local Calibration over Generic Numbers: Rather than consuming NASA FIRMS or the Canadian FWI as black-box numbers, WillAI scientifically adapts their formulas to high-altitude Andean grasses (ichu and pajonal), reducing prediction error by 39.8%.
  • Solving the "Last Mile" Problem: The most advanced satellite telemetry is useless if mountain comuneros cannot understand the alerts or report fires without 4G. WillAI connects NASA space data directly to ancestral Quechua-speaking pastoralists through offline edge computing.
  • Infrastructure-Aware Propagation Modeling: Unlike typical planar fire models, WillAI's Dijkstra engine embeds local infrastructure (91 mountain roads and rivers) as dynamic travel barriers, simulating real Andean firefighting tactics.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Extreme Topography: Andean slopes regularly exceed 45∘45^\circ45∘, where uphill flame propagation accelerates exponentially due to radiative preheating.
  • Severe Digital Divide: Complete absence of telecommunications outside Coracora's urban core required an uncompromising offline-first architecture.
  • Cultural & Communal Governance: Recognition that communal brigades (brigadas comunales) are the true first responders, necessitating native-language respect and non-bureaucratic workflows.
  • Ecological Fragility: High Andean bofedal peat soils store enormous volumes of carbon and water; once burned, they require centuries to regenerate.
